questions.question: A company wants a CI/CD pipeline that builds code from a Git repository, runs tests, and deploys to ECS on every commit with managed services. Which combination fits?
options: AWS Config and AWS CloudTrail.
AWS CodePipeline with AWS CodeBuild for build/test and an ECS (rolling or blue/green) deploy action.
Amazon SQS and AWS Lambda.
AWS Backup and AWS DataSync.
questions.explanation: CodePipeline orchestrates stages, CodeBuild compiles and tests, and ECS deploy actions release. The other combinations are not CI/CD services.

questions.question: A team deploys Lambda functions and wants to shift 10% of traffic to a new version for 10 minutes and automatically roll back if an error alarm triggers. What should be used?
options: Overwrite $LATEST and monitor manually.
Create a second function and switch API Gateway integration manually.
Lambda aliases with weighted traffic shifting managed by a canary deployment configuration (for example AWS SAM/CodeDeploy Canary10Percent10Minutes) with CloudWatch alarm rollback.
Use Lambda reserved concurrency set to 10%.
questions.explanation: Alias traffic shifting with canary deployments and alarms enables automatic rollback. Overwriting $LATEST has no rollback. Manual switching is slow and error-prone. Reserved concurrency limits concurrency, it does not split traffic.

questions.question: A team needs to store application configuration flags that can be changed at runtime with validation and gradual rollout. Which service is designed for this?
options: AWS Secrets Manager.
An Amazon S3 static website hosting a JSON config file.
AWS AppConfig (part of Systems Manager).
AWS CloudFormation outputs.
questions.explanation: AppConfig supports feature flags, validators, deployment strategies, and automatic rollback on alarms. Secrets Manager is for secrets. S3 lacks validation and rollout control. CloudFormation outputs are static stack values.

questions.question: A company needs a standardized, approved set of CloudFormation-based products that developers can self-provision with governance constraints. Which service fits?
options: AWS Organizations tag policies combined with service control policies.
AWS Service Catalog portfolios and products with launch constraints.
AWS Budgets.
AWS CloudShell.
questions.explanation: Service Catalog lets admins publish approved IaC products with constraints (launch roles, parameters) for self-service. Tag policies standardize tags. Budgets track cost. CloudShell is a browser shell.

questions.question: An operations team wants to run a shell command on 500 EC2 instances without SSH. Which feature should they use?
options: EC2 Instance Connect for each instance.
Systems Manager Run Command.
AWS Batch.
CloudFormation custom resources.
questions.explanation: Run Command executes documents across fleets using tags or resource groups with auditing. Instance Connect is interactive per instance. Batch runs jobs, not commands on existing instances. Custom resources run during stack operations.

questions.question: A company wants to be notified proactively about AWS scheduled maintenance events affecting its instances across all accounts and route them to a ticketing system. What should they use?
options: CloudTrail management events.
AWS Health organizational view with EventBridge rules forwarding Health events to the ticketing integration.
Amazon Inspector findings.
AWS Config rules.
questions.explanation: AWS Health publishes account-specific events (including scheduled maintenance) and organizational view aggregates them; EventBridge routes them. CloudTrail captures API calls. Inspector and Config are unrelated to AWS maintenance.

questions.question: Which Well-Architected pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems and continually improving processes and procedures?
options: Reliability.
Performance Efficiency.
Operational Excellence.
Sustainability.
questions.explanation: Operational Excellence covers operations, observability, and continuous improvement (e.g., IaC, small frequent changes, learning from failures). Reliability is about recovering and meeting demand. Performance Efficiency is resource selection. Sustainability minimizes environmental impact.

questions.question: A team uses CDK and wants to prevent deployments that violate security rules (e.g., public S3 buckets) before resources are created. What approach fits BEST?
options: Rely on AWS Config detective rules after deployment.
Review the CloudTrail logs weekly.
Use Amazon Inspector.
Use CDK Aspects/cdk-nag or CloudFormation Guard and CloudFormation Hooks to validate templates proactively (and Control Tower proactive controls).
questions.explanation: Proactive validation with cdk-nag, Guard rules, and Hooks blocks noncompliant resources before provisioning. Config detects after creation. CloudTrail review is reactive. Inspector does not evaluate IaC templates for these rules.

questions.question: A developer wants to be alerted when an Auto Scaling group fails to launch instances. Which is the simplest option?
options: Configure an EventBridge rule for EC2 Auto Scaling "EC2 Instance Launch Unsuccessful" events (or ASG SNS notifications).
Enable VPC Flow Logs.
Query CloudTrail Lake daily.
Use AWS Cost Explorer.
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling emits lifecycle events to EventBridge and can publish SNS notifications. Flow Logs, CloudTrail Lake daily queries, and Cost Explorer are not timely or relevant.

questions.question: A regulated company wants runbooks for common incidents (e.g., restart service, isolate instance) to be executed consistently with approvals and auditing. What should be used?
options: Systems Manager Automation runbooks (with approval steps) triggered from Incident Manager or EventBridge.
Wiki pages with manual steps.
Lambda functions invoked from engineers laptops.
CloudFormation stack policies.
questions.explanation: SSM Automation provides codified runbooks with approval, rate control, and audit history. Manual wikis are inconsistent. Ad hoc Lambdas lack governance. Stack policies protect stack resources from updates.

questions.question: An application team wants metrics about memory utilization on EC2 instances, which are not available by default. What should they do?
options: Enable EC2 detailed monitoring so memory metrics are published every minute.
Install the CloudWatch agent to publish memory and disk metrics.
Enable AWS Config.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor.
questions.explanation: Memory and disk utilization are OS-level metrics requiring the CloudWatch agent. Detailed monitoring increases frequency of default hypervisor metrics only. Config and Trusted Advisor do not collect memory metrics.

questions.question: A company wants to perform a Well-Architected review for a workload, track improvement items, and apply a custom lens for internal standards. Which service supports this?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor only.
AWS Audit Manager.
AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter with an OpsItem per improvement.
AWS Well-Architected Tool with custom lenses and milestones.
questions.explanation: The WA Tool guides reviews against pillars and lenses (including custom lenses) and tracks milestones and improvement plans. Trusted Advisor provides automated checks. Audit Manager maps controls to frameworks. OpsCenter manages operational issues.

questions.question: A team wants to create CloudWatch dashboards and alarms across 20 accounts in one monitoring account. Which feature should be used?
options: A separate CloudWatch dashboard in each of the 20 accounts, bookmarked by the operations team.
CloudWatch cross-account observability (monitoring account linked to source accounts).
CloudTrail organization trail.
S3 cross-Region replication.
questions.explanation: Cross-account observability lets a monitoring account view metrics, logs, and traces from source accounts. Separate dashboards fragment visibility. CloudTrail and S3 replication do not provide metrics dashboards.

questions.question: A company deploys microservices on ECS and wants blue/green deployments with automated rollback based on alarms, without managing CodeDeploy separately. What should be used?
options: Rolling updates with minimumHealthyPercent 0.
Manually creating a new service and switching DNS.
Native Amazon ECS blue/green deployments (built into the ECS deployment controller) with lifecycle hooks and CloudWatch alarm rollback.
ECS Exec.
questions.explanation: ECS added native blue/green deployments in 2025 with bake time, lifecycle hooks, and alarm-based rollback. Rolling with 0% healthy causes downtime. Manual DNS switching is slow. ECS Exec is for shell access.

questions.question: An organization wants to centralize log retention settings and ensure new log groups have a 90-day retention. Which option works?
options: Rely on the default of never expire.
Delete logs manually monthly.
Enable VPC Flow Logs.
Use CloudWatch Logs account-level policies or an AWS Config rule with remediation to set retention on new log groups.
questions.explanation: Config rules (e.g., cw-loggroup-retention-period-check) with remediation, or account policies, enforce retention consistently. Never-expire increases costs. Manual deletion is error-prone. Flow Logs are unrelated.

questions.question: A team wants to detect anomalies in application metrics without manually setting static thresholds that change with weekly seasonality. What should they use?
options: Static threshold alarms that engineers update by hand each week.
AWS Budgets.
AWS Config conformance packs.
CloudWatch anomaly detection alarms based on a trained band.
questions.explanation: Anomaly detection models metric patterns including seasonality and alarms outside the expected band. Hand-updated thresholds are toil. Budgets and Config are unrelated.

questions.question: Which AWS service records configuration changes and relationships between resources, allowing you to see what a security group looked like last week?
options: AWS Config.
Amazon CloudWatch.
AWS X-Ray.
Amazon Inspector.
questions.explanation: Config keeps a configuration history and timeline per resource. CloudWatch stores metrics and logs. X-Ray traces requests. Inspector scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: A company runs 400 accounts and wants to automatically remediate noncompliant resources, e.g., enable S3 Block Public Access, across all accounts with a single deployment. What should be used?
options: AWS Config organization rules / conformance packs with SSM Automation remediation, deployed from a delegated administrator.
A Lambda in each account deployed manually.
Trusted Advisor recommendations.
IAM Access Analyzer alone.
questions.explanation: Organization conformance packs deploy rules and remediation across all accounts centrally. Manual Lambdas do not scale. Trusted Advisor and Access Analyzer surface issues but do not auto-remediate at org scale.

questions.question: A platform team wants developers to get AI assistance for spec-driven development, generating requirements, designs, and tasks before code, using an agentic IDE. Which AWS offering fits, given Amazon Q Developer is being phased out for new sign-ups?
options: Kiro, the AWS agentic IDE/CLI for spec-driven development.
AWS CodeBuild with a buildspec that generates code from templates.
AWS CloudShell.
AWS Cloud9.
questions.explanation: Kiro is an agentic development environment built around specs (requirements, design, tasks) and hooks; AWS stopped new Q Developer sign-ups on May 15, 2026 and recommends Kiro. CodeBuild is a build service. CloudShell is a browser terminal. Cloud9 is no longer available to new customers.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate 300 on-premises VMware VMs to EC2 quickly with minimal changes and minimal downtime cutover. Which service is BEST?
options: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) for rehosting with continuous block-level replication.
AWS DMS.
AWS DataSync.
AWS Snowball Edge for each VM.
questions.explanation: MGN performs lift-and-shift with continuous replication and short cutover windows, launching test and cutover instances. DMS migrates databases. DataSync moves files and objects. Snowball is offline bulk transfer, not VM rehosting with minimal downtime.

questions.question: A company must migrate an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime. Which combination should be used?
options: AWS DataSync to copy the data files.
Application Migration Service to rehost the database server.
Export all tables to CSV files and bulk import them into Aurora PostgreSQL with psql during a weekend outage.
AWS DMS Schema Conversion (or AWS SCT) to convert the schema, and AWS DMS full load plus CDC for data.
questions.explanation: Heterogeneous migrations need schema conversion plus DMS full load and ongoing change data capture for minimal downtime. DataSync copies files, not database transactions. MGN rehosts Oracle as-is on EC2 rather than converting. CSV export requires long downtime.

questions.question: A company that has never used AWS Snow devices needs to move 500 TB from its data center, where the 1 Gbps internet link is already heavily used, and must finish within 3 weeks. What is the BEST approach in 2026?
options: Order AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices.
Use AWS DataSync over the existing 1 Gbps link.
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration from the data center.
Copy the data to company-owned storage devices and upload it at high speed at an AWS Data Transfer Terminal location, then validate in S3.
questions.explanation: A dedicated 1 Gbps link would need ~46 days for 500 TB, and this link is shared, so online transfer misses the deadline. Since November 7, 2025, Snowball Edge is available only to existing customers (and support ends December 31, 2026); AWS directs new customers to Data Transfer Terminal for physical transfers, DataSync for online transfers, or partners. Transfer Acceleration is still bound by the local link.

questions.question: A company wants to discover on-premises servers, collect utilization data, and plan migration waves. Which services help?
options: AWS Config.
AWS Application Discovery Service / Migration Hub (and AWS Transform for assessment) to inventory servers and plan waves.
Amazon Inspector.
AWS Budgets.
questions.explanation: Discovery tooling collects server specs, utilization, and dependencies and Migration Hub tracks migration progress; AWS Transform adds AI-driven assessment and planning. Config, Inspector, and Budgets do not inventory on-premises servers.

questions.question: A company plans a large-scale migration and wants AI agents to analyze and modernize .NET Framework applications to cross-platform .NET running on Linux, reducing Windows licensing costs. What should they use?
options: AWS Application Migration Service rehosting to Windows EC2.
AWS DMS.
AWS Elastic Beanstalk Windows platform.
AWS Transform for .NET/Windows modernization.
questions.explanation: AWS Transform uses agentic AI to port .NET Framework apps to cross-platform .NET (and modernize full Windows stacks, reported up to five times faster), removing Windows license costs. Rehosting keeps Windows licensing. DMS is for databases. Beanstalk does not refactor code.

questions.question: Which of the 7 Rs migration strategies describes moving an application to AWS with minimal changes, such as lifting a VM onto EC2?
options: Refactor.
Repurchase.
Retire.
Rehost.
questions.explanation: Rehost (lift-and-shift) moves as-is. Refactor re-architects to cloud-native. Repurchase moves to SaaS. Retire decommissions.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate an on-premises MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a few minutes of downtime. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Take a full mysqldump backup and restore it into RDS during a planned 48-hour maintenance outage window.
Use AWS Snowcone.
Use AWS Transfer Family.
Use AWS DMS (or native MySQL binlog replication) to continuously replicate to RDS, then cut over.
questions.explanation: Continuous replication lets the target stay in sync so the cutover takes minutes. Offline backup/restore incurs long downtime. Snowcone and Transfer Family are not database replication tools.

questions.question: A company needs ongoing, scheduled synchronization of 200 TB of NFS file shares to Amazon EFS and S3 with data integrity verification and bandwidth throttling. Which service fits?
options: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode.
AWS DMS.
rsync scripts on cron.
AWS DataSync with an agent on-premises.
questions.explanation: DataSync automates and accelerates transfers between NFS/SMB/HDFS/object storage and AWS storage services with integrity checks, scheduling, and throttling. Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block storage. DMS migrates databases. Custom rsync is slower and requires maintenance.

questions.question: A company wants on-premises applications to keep using SMB file shares while data is stored durably in S3 with local caching. What should be used?
options: AWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway (or FSx File Gateway for FSx for Windows).
AWS DataSync tasks scheduled every hour to copy the SMB shares into an S3 bucket.
AWS Snowball Edge.
Amazon EFS.
questions.explanation: S3 File Gateway exposes NFS/SMB shares backed by S3 with a local cache for hybrid access. DataSync is for transfers, not ongoing shares. Snowball is offline transfer. EFS is NFS for AWS-based clients.

questions.question: A partner requires uploading files to the company via SFTP, and the company wants the files to land directly in S3 without managing servers. Which service fits?
options: An EC2 instance running OpenSSH with an S3 FUSE mount.
AWS DataSync.
AWS Transfer Family (SFTP) with an S3 backend.
AWS Direct Connect.
questions.explanation: Transfer Family provides managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP/AS2 endpoints storing to S3 or EFS. A self-managed EC2 server adds ops. DataSync does not host SFTP endpoints for partners. Direct Connect is network connectivity.

questions.question: A company is migrating a mainframe COBOL application and wants AI-assisted analysis, decomposition, and refactoring to Java with automated testing, reducing modernization from years to months. What should be used?
options: AWS Transform for mainframe.
AWS Application Migration Service.
AWS Snowball Edge.
Amazon EC2 Mac instances.
questions.explanation: AWS Transform for mainframe uses AI agents for analysis, documentation, decomposition, refactoring to Java, and (from re:Invent 2025) reimagine and automated testing capabilities. MGN rehosts x86 servers, not mainframes. Snowball and Mac instances are unrelated.

questions.question: A company has an established Direct Connect link and needs to migrate 80 TB of files to S3 in one week with integrity validation. What is the MOST efficient option?
options: Snowmobile.
AWS DataSync over Direct Connect (optionally with a VPC interface endpoint).
Manual copying with the AWS CLI aws s3 sync command from an on-premises laptop.
AWS Transfer Family.
questions.explanation: DataSync over an existing high-bandwidth Direct Connect moves 80 TB efficiently with validation and parallelism. Snowmobile was for exabyte-scale and is retired. Laptop CLI copies are slow and unreliable. Transfer Family serves SFTP clients rather than bulk migration.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate hundreds of Windows and Linux servers and needs a central place to track status across multiple tools and AWS accounts. What should be used?
options: AWS Organizations.
AWS Migration Hub (with its home Region) integrated with MGN and DMS for progress tracking.
AWS Control Tower.
AWS Health.
questions.explanation: Migration Hub aggregates migration status from integrated tools across accounts. Organizations and Control Tower manage accounts and governance. Health reports AWS service events.

questions.question: A company wants to move a legacy Java application to containers without rewriting it and run it on a managed container platform. Which strategy is this?
options: Replatform (lift, tinker, and shift).
Retain.
Repurchase.
Rehost (lift and shift onto EC2 instances).
questions.explanation: Containerizing with minimal code changes to use a managed platform is replatforming. Retain keeps it on-premises. Repurchase moves to SaaS. Rehost moves as-is to VMs.

questions.question: During a migration, a company must keep on-premises Active Directory for authentication while running Windows workloads in AWS, with minimal latency. What is the recommended approach?
options: Create IAM users for every Windows user.
Deploy AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD in AWS with a trust to on-premises AD (or extend domain controllers to EC2), connected via Direct Connect/VPN.
Use Cognito user pools for domain joins.
Disable authentication until migration completes.
questions.explanation: Managed Microsoft AD with a forest trust, or DCs in AWS, gives low-latency authentication for domain-joined workloads. IAM users and Cognito cannot perform Windows domain joins. Disabling auth is unacceptable.

questions.question: A company wants a managed ActiveMQ broker after migrating from on-premises without rewriting the messaging code. Which service fits?
options: Amazon SQS.
Amazon SNS.
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams.
Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ.
questions.explanation: Amazon MQ supports ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ with standard protocols (JMS, AMQP, MQTT, STOMP), enabling lift-and-shift of messaging. SQS/SNS/Kinesis would require code changes.

questions.question: A company must migrate a 30 TB SQL Server database to AWS with the least downtime and wants to keep SQL Server features without license management. Which target and method are BEST?
options: Aurora MySQL using AWS SCT.
DynamoDB using DMS.
Amazon Redshift using COPY.
Amazon RDS for SQL Server (license-included) using native backup/restore to seed and DMS CDC (or log shipping) to catch up before cutover.
questions.explanation: RDS for SQL Server keeps engine compatibility with license-included pricing; seeding from native backups plus CDC minimizes downtime (RDS now supports up to 256 TiB storage). Converting to Aurora MySQL or DynamoDB is a re-architecture. Redshift is analytic.

questions.question: A new AWS customer needs to run AWS-managed compute and storage on premises at a factory for low-latency local processing, with the same APIs and tools as in the Region. Which service fits?
options: AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized.
AWS Outposts.
AWS Transfer Family.
Amazon WorkSpaces.
questions.explanation: Outposts extends AWS infrastructure, services, and APIs to on-premises sites and is the AWS-recommended edge compute option now that Snowball Edge is closed to new customers (since November 7, 2025). Transfer Family is managed file transfer. WorkSpaces is virtual desktops.

questions.question: A company wants to modernize a monolith incrementally, routing specific API paths to new microservices while the rest still reach the legacy app. Which pattern and AWS service combination fits?
options: Big-bang rewrite and cutover.
Retire the monolith immediately.
The strangler fig pattern using API Gateway or an ALB (or Amazon VPC Lattice) path-based routing to new services.
Rehost the monolith to a larger EC2 instance.
questions.explanation: Strangler fig incrementally replaces functionality behind a routing facade. Big-bang rewrites are risky. Retiring immediately breaks functionality. Rehosting does not modernize.

questions.question: Which migration strategy describes replacing an on-premises CRM with a SaaS product such as Salesforce?
options: Relocate.
Repurchase.
Rehost.
Refactor (re-architect).
questions.explanation: Repurchase (drop and shop) moves to a different product, often SaaS. Relocate moves VMware workloads (e.g., to Amazon EVS) without changes. Rehost moves VMs as-is. Refactor re-architects.

questions.question: A company running VMware vSphere on-premises wants to move workloads to AWS quickly while keeping VMware tools and operational model, running VCF inside its own VPC. What should it use?
options: Amazon Elastic VMware Service (Amazon EVS) — the "relocate" strategy.
AWS Application Migration Service converting all VMs to native EC2 immediately.
AWS Outposts only.
Amazon WorkSpaces.
questions.explanation: Amazon EVS (GA August 2025) runs VMware Cloud Foundation on EC2 bare metal in your VPC, enabling relocation without re-platforming. MGN converts to native EC2 (rehost), which changes the operational model. Outposts is on-premises. WorkSpaces is desktops.

questions.question: A company needs to perform a one-time migration of an on-premises PostgreSQL database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Which DMS component must they create to run the migration?
options: A DataSync agent and task.
A Storage Gateway appliance.
A DMS replication instance (or DMS Serverless replication), source and target endpoints, and a replication task.
An MGN replication server.
questions.explanation: DMS uses replication compute (instance or serverless), endpoints, and tasks. DataSync, Storage Gateway, and MGN are for files, hybrid storage, and servers respectively.

questions.question: A company migrated 200 applications and wants to reduce technical debt continuously by scanning code repositories for outdated dependencies and security issues, and autonomously remediating them. Which recent service fits?
options: AWS CodeBuild projects running custom dependency-upgrade scripts on a schedule.
AWS Config.
AWS Trusted Advisor.
AWS Transform continuous modernization (GA July 2026).
questions.explanation: AWS Transform continuous modernization connects GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, runs scheduled analyses across technical debt, security, and modernization readiness, and remediates at scale. CodeBuild needs custom logic. Config and Trusted Advisor do not analyze source code.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate on-premises file servers (Windows SMB with ACLs) to a fully managed native Windows file system in AWS. Which service fits?
options: Amazon EFS.
Amazon S3.
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server (data moved with DataSync).
Amazon FSx for Lustre with a data repository association to S3.
questions.explanation: FSx for Windows supports SMB, NTFS ACLs, and AD integration; DataSync preserves metadata during migration. EFS is NFS for Linux. S3 is object storage. Lustre is HPC.

questions.question: A company plans a migration and wants to build a business case estimating TCO savings and right-sized EC2 targets based on on-premises utilization. What should they use?
options: AWS Budgets.
AWS Cost Explorer on the empty AWS account.
Amazon Inspector.
AWS Migration Evaluator (or AWS Transform assessment) using collected on-premises utilization data.
questions.explanation: Migration Evaluator (and Transform assessments) analyze actual on-premises usage to project right-sized AWS cost and savings. Budgets and Cost Explorer operate on existing AWS spend. Inspector scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: A company wants to build a chatbot that answers questions using its internal documents stored in S3, with citations, without training a model. Which approach has the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Fine-tune a foundation model on all documents every night so answers always reflect the latest content.
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases (managed RAG) with the S3 data source and a foundation model.
Train a custom LLM from scratch on SageMaker AI.
Load all documents into the prompt for every request.
questions.explanation: Knowledge Bases manage ingestion, chunking, embedding, vector storage, and retrieval with citations. Nightly fine-tuning is costly and does not provide citations or freshness. Training from scratch is extremely expensive. Stuffing all documents exceeds context limits and cost.

questions.question: Which technique grounds a foundation model on up-to-date private data at query time without changing model weights?
options: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).
Continued pre-training.
Fine-tuning.
Model distillation.
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant context from a knowledge store and adds it to the prompt at inference time. Continued pre-training and fine-tuning change weights. Distillation trains a smaller model from a larger one.

questions.question: A bank must ensure its Bedrock-based assistant never discusses investment advice, redacts account numbers, and validates mortgage eligibility answers against written policy rules with mathematical rigor. What should be configured?
options: A detailed system prompt instructing the model to refuse investment advice, mask any account numbers, and always follow the written mortgage policy.
Bedrock Guardrails with a denied topic for investment advice, sensitive information filters for account numbers, and Automated Reasoning checks.
Provisioned Throughput for the model.
Model invocation logging to S3 with an Athena query that flags non-compliant responses for review each day.
questions.explanation: Guardrails enforce topic denial and PII redaction independent of the model, and Automated Reasoning checks formally verify answers against encoded policy rules (up to 99% verification accuracy). Prompts can be bypassed. Throughput and logging do not enforce behavior.

questions.question: A startup wants to experiment with multiple foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Meta Llama, Mistral, OpenAI open-weight) through a single API without managing infrastructure. Which service should it use?
options: Amazon SageMaker AI training jobs.
Amazon Bedrock.
Amazon Comprehend.
Amazon Rekognition.
questions.explanation: Bedrock provides serverless access to many providers foundation models through a unified API (including Converse). SageMaker training requires managing models. Comprehend and Rekognition are task-specific AI services.

questions.question: A company has built an agent with the open-source Strands Agents SDK (or LangGraph) and needs to deploy it with session isolation, long-running execution, managed memory, and secure access to internal APIs as tools. What is the MOST appropriate AWS service?
options: A single Lambda function with a 15-minute timeout that stores the conversation state and tool results in DynamoDB between calls.
Amazon Lex V2 bot.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Runtime for isolated serverless sessions, Memory, Gateway for MCP tools, and Identity.
Amazon SageMaker AI batch transform jobs that run the agent framework over queued user requests.
questions.explanation: AgentCore is framework- and model-agnostic, providing microVM session isolation, long-running sessions, managed memory, tool gateway (MCP), identity, observability, and policy. A single Lambda hits the 15-minute limit and lacks these primitives. Lex is for conversational bots. Batch transform is offline inference.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a vector store option built into Amazon S3 for storing and querying embeddings at low cost?
options: Amazon S3 Vectors (vector buckets and vector indexes).
S3 Object Lambda.
S3 Inventory.
S3 Express One Zone.
questions.explanation: S3 Vectors (GA December 2025) adds purpose-built vector buckets with indexes up to 2 billion vectors each, integrated with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and OpenSearch. The others are not vector stores.

questions.question: A company needs to extract text, tables, and form fields from millions of scanned invoices. Which service is purpose-built?
options: Amazon Comprehend.
Amazon Transcribe.
Amazon Rekognition.
Amazon Textract.
questions.explanation: Textract extracts printed/handwritten text, forms, tables, and expense/invoice fields. Comprehend performs NLP on text. Transcribe is speech-to-text. Rekognition analyzes images/video for objects and faces.

questions.question: A contact center needs to convert recorded calls into text and then detect sentiment and PII in the transcripts. Which combination fits?
options: Amazon Transcribe (with PII redaction) followed by Amazon Comprehend for sentiment (or Transcribe Call Analytics).
Amazon Polly to convert the calls to text and Amazon Translate to detect sentiment and redact PII in the transcripts.
Amazon Rekognition for the audio analysis and Amazon Textract to extract the PII and sentiment from transcripts.
Amazon Lex and Amazon Kendra.
questions.explanation: Transcribe converts speech to text and can redact PII; Comprehend analyzes sentiment and entities; Call Analytics combines both. Polly is text-to-speech. Rekognition/Textract are vision. Lex/Kendra are bots and search.

questions.question: An enterprise needs to process 5 million documents overnight with a foundation model to generate summaries, minimizing cost. Latency per request does not matter. Which approach is BEST?
options: Provisioned Throughput with a 1-month commitment sized for the overnight processing window.
On-demand InvokeModel calls from 1,000 Lambda functions.
Bedrock batch inference jobs reading input from S3 and writing output to S3.
SageMaker AI real-time endpoint on large GPUs.
questions.explanation: Batch inference is designed for large offline workloads at about half the on-demand price, handled asynchronously. Provisioned Throughput is for steady real-time traffic. Mass on-demand calls pay full price and risk throttling. Real-time GPU endpoints add management and idle cost.

questions.question: A developer wants to reduce Bedrock latency and cost for a chatbot that sends a long, identical system prompt and document context with every request. Which feature helps?
options: Bedrock Guardrails.
Model invocation logging.
Prompt caching in Amazon Bedrock.
Knowledge Base re-sync.
questions.explanation: Prompt caching caches repeated prompt prefixes, reducing latency and input token cost for cached portions. Guardrails filter content. Logging records invocations. Re-sync updates the knowledge base.

questions.question: A company wants a smaller, cheaper model that matches a large model accuracy for a narrow classification task in its domain, without labeling a large dataset. Which Bedrock capability fits?
options: Increase the max tokens parameter.
Use a larger model with a higher temperature so it generalizes better to the narrow domain task.
Bedrock model distillation (teacher-to-student) or reinforcement fine-tuning with reward functions.
Knowledge Bases with hybrid search so the model retrieves labeled examples to classify each request.
questions.explanation: Distillation uses a teacher model to generate training data for a smaller student; reinforcement fine-tuning (re:Invent 2025) improves accuracy using feedback rather than large labeled sets. Token limits and temperature do not reduce cost. Knowledge Bases address grounding, not model size.

questions.question: Which inference parameter primarily controls the randomness of a foundation model output?
options: Max tokens.
Stop sequences.
Context window.
Temperature.
questions.explanation: Higher temperature increases randomness; lower makes output more deterministic. Max tokens limits length. Stop sequences end generation. Context window is the input capacity of the model.

questions.question: A regulated company needs to ensure Bedrock traffic from its VPC never traverses the public internet and that prompts/completions are not used to train models. What should the architect state and configure?
options: Use a NAT gateway with TLS 1.3 so traffic to the Bedrock public endpoint is encrypted and stays private.
Deploy Bedrock inside the VPC subnets.
Opt out of model training by submitting a support ticket, and route traffic through a Direct Connect public VIF.
Use a Bedrock interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink); Bedrock does not use prompts or completions to train models.
questions.explanation: PrivateLink keeps traffic on the AWS network, and Bedrock data privacy commitments state inputs and outputs are not used to train models. NAT sends traffic out to public endpoints. Bedrock is a managed service, not deployed into subnets. No opt-out ticket is needed.

questions.question: A company wants a generative AI assistant for employees that connects to enterprise data sources (SharePoint, Salesforce, Slack), respects existing permissions, and can build agents and automations, without writing code. Which AWS offering fits?
options: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with a custom React chat UI and a Lambda connector written for each enterprise data source and its ACLs.
Amazon Quick (launched as Quick Suite in October 2025, evolving from QuickSight), or Amazon Q Business for enterprise Q&A.
Amazon Kendra with Lambda functions that sync each SaaS source and a custom chat front end for employees.
Amazon SageMaker AI Canvas.
questions.explanation: Amazon Quick provides agentic chat, research (Quick Research), automation (Quick Flows/Automate), and BI (Quick Sight) across enterprise connectors with permission-aware access; Amazon Q Business offers ACL-aware enterprise Q&A and can integrate with it. Building on Knowledge Bases or Kendra needs custom code and a UI. Canvas is for no-code ML models.

questions.question: An AI agent must perform actions on behalf of a signed-in user in third-party SaaS tools (e.g., create Jira tickets) using OAuth tokens, without the agent code handling raw credentials. Which capability should be used?
options: Store the OAuth refresh tokens in the agent environment variables and refresh them inside the agent code.
Use IAM users with access keys for each SaaS tool, rotated every 90 days by Secrets Manager.
Embed credentials in the system prompt.
AgentCore Identity (outbound OAuth credential providers and token vault) used by Runtime/Gateway.
questions.explanation: AgentCore Identity manages inbound authentication and outbound OAuth/API key credentials on behalf of users or the agent, keeping secrets out of code. Environment variables and prompts expose secrets. IAM users do not authenticate to SaaS tools.

questions.question: Which model family is Amazon own set of foundation models available on Bedrock, including a speech-to-speech model and a fast reasoning model with a 1M-token context?
options: Amazon Titan Text G1 only.
Amazon Lex.
Amazon Nova (for example Nova 2 Lite and Nova 2 Sonic).
Amazon Polly Neural.
questions.explanation: Amazon Nova 2 (re:Invent 2025) includes Nova 2 Lite (reasoning, 1M-token context), Nova 2 Sonic (speech-to-speech), and Nova 2 Omni (preview). Titan G1 is an older family. Lex and Polly are not foundation model families.

questions.question: A retailer wants to evaluate the quality of its RAG application responses (faithfulness, relevance, citation accuracy) automatically before each release. What should be used?
options: CloudWatch CPU and latency metrics on the application, with alarms when p99 response time increases.
Amazon Bedrock Evaluations (RAG evaluation with LLM-as-a-judge), or AgentCore Evaluations.
AWS X-Ray service maps that trace each retrieval and generation call and score their quality.
Amazon Inspector.
questions.explanation: Bedrock Evaluations assess RAG retrieval and generation quality with LLM-as-a-judge and built-in metrics; AgentCore Evaluations monitor agent quality continuously. CPU metrics, tracing maps, and vulnerability scans do not measure answer quality.

questions.question: A company wants to train and deploy its own custom ML model (XGBoost) with managed training, hyperparameter tuning, and hosted endpoints. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Bedrock.
Amazon Comprehend (pre-trained NLP).
Amazon SageMaker AI.
AWS Glue.
questions.explanation: SageMaker AI provides managed training, tuning, and hosting for custom models. Bedrock focuses on foundation models. Comprehend is a pre-trained NLP service. Glue is ETL.

questions.question: A team building an agent needs to give it reliable access to the web for grounding and to interact with websites (fill forms) in an isolated environment. Which AgentCore capabilities fit?
options: AgentCore Memory only.
AgentCore Browser (managed, isolated browser) plus the AgentCore web search tool via Gateway.
A NAT gateway from a Lambda function running a headless Chromium layer to browse and fill in forms.
Amazon CloudFront.
questions.explanation: AgentCore Browser provides a secure cloud browser for agents to navigate and interact with sites, and managed web search (GA Summit NY 2026) provides grounding. Memory stores context. Self-hosted headless browsers in Lambda are brittle. CloudFront is a CDN.

questions.question: A developer notices a model producing confident but incorrect facts. What is this phenomenon called and a common mitigation?
options: Overfitting; mitigate by training with larger batch sizes and more epochs on the same data.
Latency; mitigate with Provisioned Throughput so the model has time to verify its facts.
Drift; mitigate with more GPU memory.
Hallucination; mitigate with RAG grounding, citations, and contextual grounding checks.
questions.explanation: Hallucinations are fabricated outputs; grounding with retrieved context and contextual grounding checks reduce them. The other pairs describe unrelated concepts or mitigations.

questions.question: A company needs consistent, guaranteed model throughput for a high-volume production application with steady traffic on a custom fine-tuned model in Bedrock. Which option is required?
options: Bedrock batch inference.
Cross-Region inference profiles only, spreading requests across Regions for more capacity.
Bedrock Provisioned Throughput (model units) purchased for the custom model.
Prompt caching only.
questions.explanation: Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated model units for consistent performance and historically is required to serve most custom models. Batch is offline. Cross-Region inference increases available capacity for on-demand base models but does not guarantee throughput. Prompt caching reduces tokens but not guaranteed capacity.

questions.question: A company wants its on-demand Bedrock traffic to automatically use capacity in multiple Regions to handle bursts. What should it use?
options: Route 53 latency routing to Bedrock endpoints.
Global Accelerator in front of the Bedrock Regional endpoints.
Cross-Region inference profiles (geographic or global).
Bedrock Knowledge Bases.
questions.explanation: Cross-Region inference routes requests across Regions within a geography (or globally) to increase throughput and resilience without extra cost. Route 53 and Global Accelerator are not used with Bedrock APIs this way. Knowledge Bases are for RAG.

questions.question: A company wants an AI-assisted migration of hundreds of applications, including VMware discovery, wave planning, and network conversion, using agentic AI. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases loaded with the VMware inventory exports.
AWS Config.
Amazon SageMaker AI Canvas.
AWS Transform (for VMware and other migration/modernization jobs).
questions.explanation: AWS Transform uses specialized agents for VMware migrations (discovery, dependency mapping, wave planning, network translation), mainframe, .NET, and custom modernization. The others do not automate migrations.

questions.question: Which service identifies objects, faces, text, and unsafe content in images and videos?
options: Amazon Textract.
Amazon Comprehend Medical.
Amazon Transcribe.
Amazon Rekognition.
questions.explanation: Rekognition provides image and video analysis including labels, faces, text in images, and moderation. Textract is document extraction. Comprehend is NLP. Transcribe is speech-to-text.

questions.question: A company wants a human-in-the-loop approval before an AI agent executes high-risk actions (e.g., issuing refunds over $500). Which design aligns with AWS guidance for responsible agentic AI?
options: Let the agent decide autonomously, with a system prompt that lists the refund rules and asks it to double-check any refund above $500 before calling the tool.
Increase the model temperature so it considers more alternatives and becomes more cautious about high-risk refunds.
Rely on CloudWatch alarms that page the finance team after refunds over $500 are issued so they can be reversed.
Route the action through a Step Functions approval step (wait for task token) plus AgentCore Policy on the tool, with audit logging.
questions.explanation: Human oversight workflows with approval mechanisms (e.g., Step Functions task tokens) are explicitly called out in the SAP-C02 emerging topics, alongside Guardrails and AgentCore Identity; policy-enforced tool boundaries add defense in depth. Prompts and temperature are not controls. Alarms after the fact are detective only.

questions.question: A company has 30 VPCs across multiple accounts and on-premises networks connected via VPN. They need transitive routing between all VPCs and on-premises with centralized management. What should they use?
options: AWS Transit Gateway with VPC attachments and a VPN (or Direct Connect gateway) attachment, shared via AWS RAM.
Full-mesh VPC peering between all 30 VPCs, with a VPN connection terminated in each VPC for on-premises access.
A single shared VPC with many subnets, one per team, shared across accounts.
Internet gateways with public IPs.
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway is a Regional hub supporting transitive routing among thousands of attachments with route tables for segmentation. VPC peering is non-transitive and a 30-VPC mesh requires 435 connections. Consolidating into one VPC breaks account isolation. Internet paths are insecure.

questions.question: Which statement about VPC peering is correct?
options: VPC peering supports transitive routing, so traffic can flow through a hub VPC to other peered VPCs.
VPC peering requires an internet gateway in both VPCs to exchange traffic.
VPC peering only works between VPCs in the same account and the same Region.
VPC peering is non-transitive and does not support overlapping CIDR blocks.
questions.explanation: Peering connects two VPCs directly (cross-account and cross-Region supported) with no transitivity and no overlapping CIDRs. It does not use internet gateways.

questions.question: A company needs a dedicated, private, consistent-latency connection from its data center to AWS with 10 Gbps bandwidth. What should it use?
options: AWS Direct Connect (dedicated connection).
AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet using two IPsec tunnels.
AWS Client VPN endpoints for the data center servers.
AWS Global Accelerator with static anycast IPs.
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides private dedicated connectivity (1, 10, 100, and 400 Gbps dedicated ports) with consistent performance. Site-to-Site VPN traverses the internet (up to 1.25 Gbps per tunnel standard, higher with large-bandwidth tunnels). Client VPN is for users. Global Accelerator improves internet routing to AWS endpoints.

questions.question: A company requires encrypted, highly resilient hybrid connectivity using Direct Connect and wants to protect against a single device or location failure. Which design follows AWS maximum resiliency recommendations?
options: A single 100 Gbps Direct Connect dedicated connection with MACsec encryption enabled.
Two Direct Connect connections terminating on the same device at one DX location with MACsec.
A Site-to-Site VPN only, using two IPsec tunnels over the internet.
Two Direct Connect connections at each of two separate DX locations (four connections) terminating on separate devices, with MACsec or IPsec VPN over DX for encryption.
questions.explanation: Maximum resiliency uses separate connections terminating on separate devices in more than one location; MACsec (layer 2) or IPsec over DX adds encryption. A single connection or single location is a failure point. VPN-only lacks consistent performance.

questions.question: A SaaS provider wants to expose its service privately to hundreds of customer VPCs without VPC peering and with overlapping CIDRs allowed. What should be used?
options: AWS PrivateLink: a VPC endpoint service fronted by a Network Load Balancer, consumed via interface endpoints.
A VPC peering connection with each customer VPC, with route tables limited to the service subnet and security groups per customer.
A Transit Gateway shared with all customers through AWS RAM and one route table per customer.
Public ALB with IP allow lists.
questions.explanation: PrivateLink exposes services through interface endpoints in consumer VPCs; traffic is unidirectional and overlapping CIDRs do not matter. Peering and TGW require non-overlapping CIDRs and broader network access. Public ALB uses the internet.

questions.question: A company has microservices across many VPCs and accounts running on EC2, ECS, EKS, and Lambda, and wants service-to-service connectivity with IAM-based auth policies and no need to manage routing or overlapping CIDRs. Which service fits BEST?
options: Transit Gateway with route tables per service.
Full-mesh VPC peering.
A self-managed service mesh on EC2.
Amazon VPC Lattice service networks.
questions.explanation: VPC Lattice provides application-layer service networking across VPCs/accounts with auth policies, works with overlapping CIDRs, and supports multiple compute types. TGW and peering work at the network layer and require CIDR planning. A self-managed mesh adds operational burden.

questions.question: A company wants to resolve on-premises DNS names from its VPCs and resolve private hosted zone records from on-premises. What should be configured?
options: Create public hosted zones for the internal names and restrict who can query them with DNSSEC signing and TTLs.
Configure DHCP option sets that point VPC instances to a public resolver such as 8.8.8.8.
Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints with forwarding rules to on-premises DNS, and inbound endpoints for on-premises to query VPC DNS.
Route DNS traffic through a NAT gateway to the on-premises DNS servers.
questions.explanation: Resolver endpoints enable hybrid DNS: outbound forwards VPC queries to on-premises; inbound accepts queries from on-premises. Public zones expose internal names. External resolvers cannot resolve private zones. NAT does not provide DNS forwarding.

questions.question: A global enterprise wants to build and manage a unified WAN connecting multiple AWS Regions, branch offices via SD-WAN, and data centers, using a central policy for segmentation. Which service fits BEST?
options: Multiple Transit Gateways peered manually with static routes.
AWS Cloud WAN with a core network policy and segments.
A single VPC spanning Regions.
AWS Client VPN.
questions.explanation: Cloud WAN provides a managed global network with policy-based segmentation and automatic routing across Regions and on-premises attachments. Manually peered TGWs work but require more management. VPCs are Regional. Client VPN is for individual users.

questions.question: A private subnet EC2 instance needs to download OS updates from the internet but must not accept inbound connections from the internet. What should be used?
options: An internet gateway route (0.0.0.0/0) in the private subnet route table.
A VPC gateway endpoint configured for the OS update repositories.
A NAT gateway (zonal in a public subnet, or regional mode) with a default route from the private subnet.
An egress-only internet gateway configured for IPv4 traffic from the private subnet to the internet.
questions.explanation: NAT gateways enable outbound IPv4 internet access without allowing inbound connections; zonal NAT gateways live in a public subnet, while regional NAT gateways (Nov 2025) need no public subnet. An IGW route makes the subnet public. Gateway endpoints only reach S3/DynamoDB. Egress-only IGWs are for IPv6.

questions.question: Which Route 53 routing policy should be used to direct users to the Region with the lowest network latency?
options: Geolocation routing.
Weighted routing.
Latency-based routing.
Multivalue answer routing.
questions.explanation: Latency routing returns the record for the Region with the lowest measured latency to the user. Geolocation routes by user location regardless of latency. Weighted splits by percentage. Multivalue returns multiple healthy records.

questions.question: A company must route all VPC egress internet traffic through a centralized firewall fleet of third-party virtual appliances with automatic scaling and high availability. Which service is designed for inserting such appliances?
options: An Application Load Balancer with the firewall appliances registered as IP targets.
A Network Load Balancer with sticky sessions routing traffic to the appliance fleet.
Gateway Load Balancer with GWLB endpoints in the spoke/egress VPC routes.
A Classic Load Balancer in TCP mode in front of the firewall instances.
questions.explanation: GWLB uses GENEVE encapsulation to transparently send traffic to appliance fleets while preserving flows, scaling and health-checking appliances. ALB/NLB/CLB are not designed for transparent bump-in-the-wire inspection.

questions.question: A company wants to reach an AWS service such as SQS privately from a VPC without internet access. Which endpoint type should be used?
options: An interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) for SQS with private DNS enabled.
A gateway VPC endpoint for SQS added to the private subnet route tables with an endpoint policy.
A NAT gateway in a public subnet with a route from the private subnet.
A VPC peering connection to the AWS-managed SQS service VPC.
questions.explanation: Most AWS services are reached privately via interface endpoints. Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB. NAT sends traffic to public endpoints. There is no SQS VPC to peer with.

questions.question: A company is running out of IPv4 addresses in its VPCs and EKS clusters. Which strategy BEST addresses this long-term?
options: Create more VPCs that reuse the same overlapping 10.0.0.0/16 CIDR and connect them with NAT between each VPC.
Assign public IPv4 addresses to all pods and nodes so private address space is no longer consumed.
Recreate all subnets as smaller /28 subnets so addresses are allocated more efficiently across AZs.
Adopt IPv6 (dual-stack or IPv6-only subnets, EKS IPv6 clusters) and use Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) for planning; add secondary CIDRs (e.g., 100.64.0.0/10) as a near-term fix.
questions.explanation: IPv6 removes address scarcity and IPAM helps manage allocation; secondary CIDRs relieve pressure short-term. Overlapping CIDRs complicate routing. Public IPv4 addresses are charged hourly (since February 2024) and scarce. Smaller subnets reduce available IPs further.

questions.question: An application needs static IPs for allow-listing by partners and a global entry point that improves TCP performance to an ALB in two Regions. What should be used?
options: CloudFront with Lambda@Edge routing each request to the closest Regional ALB origin.
AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups in each Region pointing to the ALBs.
Route 53 geolocation routing with records for each Regional ALB.
Elastic IP addresses attached to each ALB in both Regions.
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IPs and routes over the AWS backbone to healthy Regional endpoints. CloudFront IPs are not static. Route 53 provides DNS, not static IPs. ALBs do not support Elastic IPs.

questions.question: Two VPCs in different accounts both use 10.0.0.0/16 and an application in one must call an API in the other. What is the SIMPLEST solution?
options: Create a VPC peering connection between the two VPCs and update both route tables.
Attach both VPCs to a Transit Gateway using default route table association and propagation for the 10.0.0.0/16 routes.
Expose the API via PrivateLink (endpoint service with NLB) or VPC Lattice, which do not require non-overlapping CIDRs.
Re-IP one of the VPCs immediately to a non-overlapping CIDR and then peer them.
questions.explanation: PrivateLink and VPC Lattice work across overlapping CIDRs. Peering and TGW routing require distinct CIDRs (TGW could work with NAT but is complex). Re-IPing is disruptive.

questions.question: What is the purpose of VPC Flow Logs?
options: To capture IP traffic metadata (accepted/rejected flows) for network interfaces, subnets, or VPCs for troubleshooting and security analysis.
To capture full packet payloads for deep packet inspection.
To record AWS API calls made against VPC resources for auditing.
To block malicious traffic automatically based on flow patterns.
questions.explanation: Flow Logs record flow metadata (source, destination, ports, action) to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Firehose. Full packets require Traffic Mirroring. API calls are in CloudTrail. Flow Logs do not block traffic.

questions.question: A company wants to centrally filter outbound DNS queries from all VPCs to block known malicious domains. Which service provides this?
options: AWS WAF web ACLs associated with each VPC to block requests to malicious domains.
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall with managed domain lists, deployed via Firewall Manager across accounts.
Security groups with outbound rules that deny traffic to specific domain names.
Amazon GuardDuty only, which automatically blocks DNS queries from VPCs to known malicious domains.
questions.explanation: DNS Firewall filters DNS queries from VPCs using allow/deny domain lists, including AWS managed threat lists. WAF does not attach to VPCs. Security groups cannot filter domains. GuardDuty detects but does not block DNS queries.

questions.question: A company wants to connect a remote office to its VPC quickly over the internet with encryption. Which option is fastest to set up?
options: AWS Site-to-Site VPN with a virtual private gateway or Transit Gateway.
An AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection ordered from a DX location near the office.
A VPC peering connection from the office network to the VPC.
An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service exposed to the office network.
questions.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN can be established in minutes over the internet with IPsec. Direct Connect takes weeks. Peering and PrivateLink connect VPCs/services, not on-premises offices.

questions.question: A company uses a Direct Connect connection to access public AWS services such as S3 public endpoints and also private VPCs across multiple Regions. Which virtual interfaces and gateways should be used?
options: A public VIF for AWS public endpoints, and a transit VIF to a Direct Connect gateway associated with Transit Gateways in multiple Regions (or private VIFs to a DX gateway for VGWs).
A single private VIF directly attached to one VPC virtual private gateway, reused for public service traffic.
A public VIF for all traffic, including private IP traffic to VPCs in multiple Regions.
A hosted VPN connection only, running IPsec over the internet to each Region.
questions.explanation: Public VIFs reach AWS public IP space; transit VIFs via DX gateway connect to TGWs across Regions. A single private VIF reaches one VGW/VPC. Public VIFs cannot reach private VPC IPs. VPN alone does not use DX.

questions.question: A company wants to host a public website on CloudFront with a custom domain at the zone apex (example.com). Which Route 53 record should be used?
options: An alias A (and AAAA) record pointing to the CloudFront distribution.
A CNAME record at the zone apex pointing to the CloudFront distribution domain name.
An MX record at the apex that points to the CloudFront distribution.
A TXT record containing the CloudFront distribution domain name.
questions.explanation: Alias records can map the zone apex to AWS resources like CloudFront, and alias queries to AWS resources are free. CNAMEs are not allowed at the apex. MX and TXT records are for mail and verification.
